# Retained GUI fixtures

These fixtures belong to Nona and exercise stage 2 of #664. They are not the
interactive desktop acceptance application for stage 4.

Stage 3's `controls.mjs` and `drive-controls.py` exercise native controls,
AT-SPI roles/names, Unicode text, folder selection/cancellation and close/reopen
with background timers, Promises and child stdout. X11 additionally injects
pointer and keyboard input through XTest/xdotool. The driver retains raw output
and accessibility snapshots per backend/scale/GC mode under
`work/gui-evidence/controls-*`. These are configured tests, not a claim that
this Windows checkout has run a Linux desktop or a real IME session.

- `layout.json`: independently specified logical bounds at 200×120 and 240×160.
- `pixels.json`: analytically specified interior ARGB pixels for clipping,
  drawing and the image, replayed by real Cairo at device scales 1 and 2.
  Text checks use an ink-area bound instead of requiring identical rasterizer
  antialiasing across graphics-library releases.
- `pixels.png`: Nona's 2×2 red/green/blue/white RGBA image, reproducible with
  `node tests/fixtures/gui/make-pixels.mjs`.
- `Abel-Regular.ttf`: Abel from the [Google Fonts repository](https://github.com/google/fonts/tree/3b99d83d2625944fc0b8bd328d793fa819b92381/ofl/abel),
  pinned to commit `3b99d83d2625944fc0b8bd328d793fa819b92381`.
  SHA-256: `8809dcad25318225052f88333e208c5aad4adcb7b2c934c135735ec19aa410b4`.
  Distributed under the adjacent [SIL Open Font License](OFL.txt).
- `retained.mjs`: bounded rendering, update, resize, scrolling, removal and
  close/reopen fixture. Copy the font and PNG beside the built executable.

`tests/gui-elements.test.ts` runs wrapper and executable native doubles on
Windows/Linux x64 in both compiler GC modes. With `NONA_GTK_GUI_TESTS=1` on
Linux x64 and a display, it additionally compares real Cairo replay with
`pixels.json`, checks local font/image loading and failed-load rollback, and
captures before/after removal and reopening. Capture helpers exist only in
test composition. The checked-in expected values are never regenerated by
the production layout or rendering implementation.
